title: Black rot on cabbage (uozo mweusi wa kabichi) - Kenya

Header: Black rot on cabbage (uozo mweusi wa kabichi) - Kenya

Prevention: Rotate with non-brassicas like maize and beans, onions and pumpkins for at least 2 years
Keep field free from weeds to avoid alternate host of the
Avoid weeding during wet conditions to avoid spread on inoculums
Apply mulch to avoid disease spread by rain splash
After harvest remove all the plant debris
Do not allow machinery and equipment movement from infested to non-infested fields
Monitoring: In the nursery look out for a yellow appearance along the margin of the cotyledon which later shrivel and drop off.
The affected seedlings turn yellow to brown wilt and die.
On the mature plant look out for: 1.
Yellow, brown or black v-shaped patches at the edge of the leaves; 2.
Black veins when the yellow black lesions are held against light; 3.
A black ring in a cross- section of the stem
In later stages, check out for blackheads with an offensive foul smell
Disease is common during wet conditions with high temperatures
Take immediate action when first symptoms appear
Direct Control: Remove all infected plants and debris from the field and destroy by burning
Spray the remaining healthy plants using a copper- based protective fungicide to supress further damage (e.g.
Restrictions: II (Moderately hazardous9; Spray interval of 14 days during wet weather; PHI 7 days; Use a maximum of 3 sprays; When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
